source.body_text: In the 9th century, Baghdad had cheques, bills of exchange, international money transfers, and venture capital, all without interest. Explore how Caliph Harun al-Rashid built the world's first multicultural economic hub, how Abu Yusuf revolutionized tax policy, and how the hawala system moved money across continents on trust alone. Topics: Abbasid Baghdad, Harun al-Rashid, Abu Yusuf, Sakk & Suftaja, Hawala, Mudaraba Series: Historical Islamic Economics (Part I) • Episode 3 of 6

short_video.voiceover: Most people think ancient banking was primitive. But in the 9th century, Baghdad had cheques, international money transfers, and venture capital. All without interest. Caliph Harun al-Rashid built the world's first multicultural economic hub. The hawala system moved money across continents on trust alone. A merchant could write a cheque in Baghdad and cash it in Canton, four thousand miles away. The House of Wisdom wasn't just about translating books. It was about reimagining commerce itself.
